card.title: The time between booking a venue tour and arriving deserves a plan
card.series: Ad Leads Aren't Worse Than Referrals. They're Just Colder.
card.audience: Venue owners investing in visibility who want to carry a couple's interest through to the in-person tour.
card.why_selected: This is the strongest offer-led scene because it shows WIA considering the couple's experience and the venue's real schedule together. It gives LeadLock a clear role while preserving the owner's role in sales. Its central point is pre-tour interest, distinct from the recent content about visibility, attribution and time away from Instagram.
card.wia_in_action: WIA reviewed the inquiry-to-tour journey and asked about the venue's existing virtual-tour option. Whitney proposed an earlier phone or virtual connection for couples whose in-person visit was further away. Fallon Looney, who was on the historical call and is no longer with WIA, suggested a supplemental email with wedding footage and an invitation to ask questions. The recommendations respected the owner's tour schedule rather than asking her to add more tour hours.
card.why_it_matters: An owner may think, 'They've booked the tour, so now we'll send reminders.' This scene adds another question: what would help that couple stay interested and feel more familiar with the venue? It demonstrates Whitney's belief that automation should 'enhance the sales process, not replace it.'
evidence_points: The WIA team proposed reviewing the language and personalization of nurture between inquiry and tour.
The venue owner said some couples schedule further ahead to accommodate family and described limits on when the venue can host tours.
Whitney asked whether virtual tours were already an option, and the owner said they were.
Whitney proposed an earlier personal connection; Fallon proposed a supplemental email for couples with a longer wait.
card.core_perspective: When a couple schedules a tour a few weeks away, there's an opportunity to help them picture their wedding before they arrive. We look at what happens during that wait, including the emails they receive and where a personal conversation would help.
card.offer_connection: Connect this to LeadLock and The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage: WIA builds automated email and text follow-up that supports the owner's personal sales conversations. The scene makes the value of pre-consult nurture concrete without presenting the proposed virtual contact or supplemental email as an implemented feature. Close the Instagram piece with an invitation to inquire about LeadLock.
verify_before_publishing: Approve an anonymized account of this historical call; credit Whitney's suggestion and do not present Fallon as current staff.
Keep both follow-up ideas as recommendations, with no cancellation figures, implementation claims or results.

card.title: I want to know what made a couple book, as well as what they loved afterward
card.series: Watch Us Build an Ad Strategy
card.audience: Wedding pros with strong reviews who want their advertising to reflect why their best-fit couples chose them.
card.why_selected: This earns the reach piece through a clear founder perspective rather than a forced polarizing hook. It differs from the recent UVP training: the point is which customer evidence WIA wants and why, rather than the general importance of positioning before campaign setup.
card.wia_in_action: During a strategy call, Whitney explained that WIA asks ELEVATE clients for existing buying research. She proposed collecting feedback from newly booked couples and using what WIA learns to inform ad copy and landing pages. The WIA move is customer research tied to a specific advertising decision.
card.why_it_matters: An owner may think, 'Our reviews already tell you why couples love us.' Whitney's question makes room for another kind of evidence: what mattered before the wedding happened. It supports her belief that 'good marketing decisions start with good data' without dismissing reviews or claiming an industry-wide research gap.
evidence_points: Whitney said WIA asks new ELEVATE clients whether they have market research to share.
She distinguished reviews from research into buying triggers.
She proposed asking newly signed clients about their decision and feeding that information back into ad copy and landing pages.
The call does not report survey responses or changes made from that research.
card.core_perspective: I want to understand what a couple was weighing when they chose your business. Their review can tell us what they loved about the experience. Asking about the booking decision can give us different information to consider when we write your ads.
card.offer_connection: This shows the thinking behind ELEVATE's messaging and advertising work. Keep the piece focused on the value of asking about the booking decision, with no offer CTA and no promise that a survey workflow is included or live.
verify_before_publishing: Approve use of Whitney's historical call remarks; avoid her broad characterization of wedding pros as a measured finding.
Describe the client survey and shared-data workflow as proposed, not implemented or currently included.

flags.message: Whitney does not say this in S4. A quoted belief she never expressed on the call is an invented quote.

flags.message: In S4 Whitney is floating an idea to Fallon, then a WIA team member, and asking 'pick your brain'. It does not show a client strategy call, so check how the setting is described.

flags.message: The proposal was LeadLock surveys that ELEVATE clients would have to send or tag themselves when someone signs. Whitney said the data would go into a shared spreadsheet before being woven into ad copy and landing pages. It is an unconfirmed idea, not a WIA process.

card.title: Why Carmen wanted more time and another set of eyes on a venue campaign
card.series: Watch Us Build an Ad Strategy
card.audience: Wedding venue owners who want expert guidance on what to keep running, what to review and when to make a change.
card.why_selected: The distinctive contribution is Carmen's restraint and her referral to another team expert. A dashboard lesson alone would be too basic. Combining the two scenes shows how WIA helps an owner think through a decision, with a concrete example of what guided support looks like.
card.wia_in_action: Carmen used diagnosis beyond the dashboard. She considered the limited traffic, discussed different kinds of visitor behavior and avoided claiming a cause. When a visitor reached the inquiry form and then moved away, she recommended asking Jacqueline for landing-page feedback. The scene shows support that includes judgment and collaboration, even before there is a settled answer.
card.why_it_matters: An owner may ask, 'Should we change the campaign yet?' WIA's answer depends on what there is to assess and what still needs a closer look. This shows the belief that 'good marketing decisions start with good data' through a specific decision, rather than repeating the recent attribution story.
evidence_points: Carmen said the campaign had not yet had enough breathing room for her to assess its success.
She discussed whether visitor behavior might point toward the ads or the landing-page experience, without establishing either explanation.
She noticed a visitor reaching the inquiry form and then moving away from the page.
She recommended submitting the venue's corporate landing page to Jacqueline for feedback and said she had not reached a conclusion.
card.core_perspective: We want enough evidence to make a useful recommendation. In office hours, Carmen considered how much traffic a venue campaign had received, looked at what visitors were doing after the click and recommended Jacqueline's feedback on the landing page. She kept the open questions open.
card.offer_connection: This illustrates the guided support available through the Accelerators after WIA builds and launches the campaigns. The owner continues managing the ads with expert feedback available. Keep this piece free of an offer CTA; the work itself is the trust-builder.
verify_before_publishing: Approve the anonymized office-hours scene and preserve that the campaign was for corporate events at a venue.
Do not publish the reported metrics as verified results or Carmen's preferred click count as a universal threshold.

flags.text: This illustrates the guided support available through the Accelerators after WIA builds and launches the campaigns. The owner continues managing the ads with expert feedback available.
flags.message: The scenes never say this venue is an Accelerator member or who manages the campaign. Carmen only advises posting the page for Jacqueline's feedback, so the Accelerator link is an inference.
The scenes do not name the setting as office hours. Confirm the setting before saying it publicly.

flags.text: This shows the belief that 'good marketing decisions start with good data'
flags.message: The quoted line is not in S2 or S3. It reads as a speaker's words, so present it as the card writer's framing or drop the quotation marks.

cards.review_note: D12, develop: WIA's own move (a planned connection between tour booking and the tour) on a real call; reframed so the ideas stay recommendations and no belief is quoted. Checked against the call: Whitney's suggestion is credited to her, Fallon is not presented as current staff.
